images.text: Modern computer history starts in April 1964 when IBM releases the System/360. It was the first family of computers that worked under the same architecture. This was a revolutionary invention as before, each computer had its own peripherals and applications. For achieving this new family of computers, there was a very important task that software developers had to carry out: They had to create an operating system that worked for all S/360s. The result was the OS/360. This was a very innovative software that Fred Brooks, the father of software engineering, developed with a big group of programmers.

There is another important event in the history of software engineering: the Garmisch conference in Germany. Thanks to this conference, people started to consider software development as a science and not as an art. After this, there was a change in the field of software development and it was the first time that people used the term ‘engineering' to refer to this field. Now, it was a more structured discipline and new methodologies for software development appeared. In addition, another important event took place in 1968 when IBM decides to unbundle its software. Before, there were computers that came with their own specific software, but since IBM changed the rules, companies sold pieces of software that were compatible with different computers.

This originated the environment for new companies and independent software vendors to start selling their own pieces of software. Before, there were few companies that developed software, but after IBM unbundled its software and as computers became more popular, many new companies started developing software packages that were compatible with IBM computers. This marks the beginning of the mass production of software. There were different companies that specialized in the development of particular applications or operating functions. As there were many small companies, most of them ended merging with each other to form bigger companies or groups of vendors.

There Be in Simple Past Tense Affirmative Statements
You use There was or There were in affirmative to say that something existed in the past.

We use There was or There were when we refer to the existence or presence of someone or something in the past.

You can use There was for singular and uncountable nouns, and There were for plural countable nouns.

Adjectives

Adjectives are words that describe or modify nouns. There are 2 basic positions for adjectives: before a noun and after some verbs. For this learning point, we are going to learn about adjectives that go after the verb to be.

For most cases, when we want to describe a noun, we place the adjective before that noun. However, when we use the verb to be, we place the adjective after the verb. Take a look at the next example. Here, the verb to be is followed by an adjective that describes the state of the group of people “they”.

Example:
They were happy when they worked in the software project.
Now, when we want to place a noun after the adjective, we have to start the sentence with a pronoun (there, this, it, etc.) that refers to the noun we are going to mention.

Examples:
There is an important concept we need to consider.
It is a wonderful idea!
Those were very useful pieces of software.
In these examples the pronouns there, it and those refer to the nouns that come after the adjectives concept, idea and pieces of software, respectively.
